item.title: Nurturing young minds through books

item.content:encoded:
Alotau Preparatory School marked the conclusion of National Book Week on Friday, August 7, with a colorful series of activities aimed at promoting a strong reading culture among early learners.

Located in the heart of Alotau town in Milne Bay, the school came alive as students dressed up as their favorite book characters and presented drama performances, poems, riddles, miming, and songs to wrap up the weeklong event.

This year’s National Book Week was observed across the country under the theme "Read a book, Reset your Future".

Teacher-in-Charge Muriel Israel emphasized the necessity of instilling fundamental literacy skills in young children during their early development stages.

"Keep your books close, but keep your dreams closer," Ms. Israel said. "Even though we are closing the weeklong National Book Week celebration, never close your books, as reading is every child's journey to a better life in the future."

She said reading must remain at the core of every learning environment, stating that observances such as National Book Week and Literacy Week should not be the only occasions when students are encouraged to read.

She called for reading to become a continuous daily culture rather than an isolated annual activity.

She said building a consistent reading habit in children requires active support from teachers, parents, and guardians, as daily reading provides the knowledge needed to shape a child’s future prospects.

item.title: PPC Baim appeals to residents to refrain from lawlessness
item.description: Madang's top cop, Superintendent Robert Baim, is urging all residents of Ward 8 in Madang Urban local level government to refrain from all forms of lawlessness, or they risk facing the full brunt of the law. He sounded the warning following two separate attacks on government vehicles travelling the airport road last week.
item.content:encoded:
Madang's top cop, Superintendent Robert Baim, is urging all residents of Ward 8 in Madang Urban local level government to refrain from all forms of lawlessness, or they risk facing the full brunt of the law.

He sounded the warning following two separate attacks on government vehicles travelling the airport road last week.

The first incident occurred midweek to a vehicle belonging to the PNG Maritime College and the second incident in the early hours of Saturday to a vehicle belonging to the Madang Provincial Health Authority.

In the first incident, the driver escaped near death after a bullet, penetrated the glass of the vehicle, a 15- seater bus.

The second incident around 4am on Saturday occurred near Madang Timbers, where the Madang PHA's 15-seater bus was stoned.

Superintendent Baim said police will no longer tolerate unlawful behaviours around this particular area as it is the gateway to Madang.

"Every visitor coming to Madang by air forms their perceptions about the province through Ward 8 as it is the gateway," he said.

"Whatever happens to them upon arrival around this area forms a lasting impression about Madang, and as much as possible, every resident of that area must display their best behaviour at all times.

"The first impression should reflect a province that is safe, peaceful, and welcoming."

He added that Madang's gateway should be remembered for its hospitality and not violence and criminal behaviours.

PPC Baim emphasised that all residents of ward 8, including parents and youths, must cease the habit of stoning vehicles travelling to and fro the airport in the early hours of the morning or at any time at all.

"The criminal act of stoning vehicles not only places innocent lives at risk, but also tarnishes Madang's reputation, discourages tourism and investment, and undermines economic growth and development for the province," Baim said.

item.title: Tubiana marks 125 years of faith
item.description: Archbishop of Rabaul and Metropolitan Bishop of the New Guinea Islands Rochus Tatamai has called on Catholics to renew their personal conviction, reflect on human existence, and allocate more time to prayer. Speaking during mass to conclude three days of worship for the Central Bougainville leg of the 125 Years Jubilee Celebrations at Tubiana Parish in Kieta today, Archbishop Rochus urged believer
item.content:encoded:
Archbishop of Rabaul and Metropolitan Bishop of the New Guinea Islands Rochus Tatamai has called on Catholics to renew their personal conviction, reflect on human existence, and allocate more time to prayer.

Speaking during mass to conclude three days of worship for the Central Bougainville leg of the 125 Years Jubilee Celebrations at Tubiana Parish in Kieta today, Archbishop Rochus urged believers to make themselves available for God's work.

He said while the church celebrates 125 years of history and faith in the region, there is still room for spiritual growth, emphasizing that the future of the church rests on today’s generation.

Archbishop Rochus was joined by Archbishop of Mount Hagen Clement Papa. Both leaders were invited by Bishop of the Bougainville Diocese Dariusz Kaluza to participate in the event.

Priests from local parishes and the Solomon Islands alongside catechists, deacons, religious sisters, and missionaries from across Central Bougainville attended the gathering.

A pilgrim walk from Mangkaki led into the Tubiana Mission grounds earlier in the morning, where thousands gathered for praise and worship.

The Jubilee celebrations commenced in Buin, South Bougainville, last week to mark the arrival of missionaries at Patupatuai in 1903.

The Central Bougainville leg concludes today following services at Pokpok Island on Friday to mark the 1901 arrival of missionaries, and at Mangkaki Point on Saturday, site of the first mission and parish in Bougainville.

The Catholic Church in Bougainville has since expanded to six deaneries and 35 parishes, serving a population of over 200,000 faithful.

The anniversary program now proceeds to Buka in the North region, where three weeks of celebrations will officially draw to a close.

item.title: Popondetta primary school celebrates National Book Week
item.description: Popondetta Primary School joined educational institutions across the country in celebrating National Book Week, held annually during the first week of August. Centering on this year’s theme, "Read a Book, Reset Your Future," students and teachers gathered outdoors to showcase a variety of creative activities.
item.content:encoded:
Popondetta Primary School joined educational institutions across the country in celebrating National Book Week, held annually during the first week of August.

Centering on this year’s theme, "Read a Book, Reset Your Future," students and teachers gathered outdoors to showcase a variety of creative activities.

Preparations took place throughout the week under the direction of special events coordinator Orerea Rex.

During the event, students engaged in writing short stories and original poems, creating thematic drawings, singing performance pieces, and staging short dramatic presentations.

According to Mrs Rex, the main objective of observance is to foster a strong reading culture and inspire continuous learning among students.

To keep this going, every classroom at Popondetta Primary School has established its own dedicated "library corner," stocked with books donated directly by the students themselves.

Complementing the week's festivities, Japan International Cooperation Agency [JICA] volunteer teacher Kitayama Atsuhiro spearheaded a project aimed at building custom bookshelves for each classroom at the school.

Speaking to NBC News, Mr Atsuhiro explained that funding for the initiative was provided by a Japanese organization working in partnership with sponsors from Singapore.

Following the successful implementation at Popondetta Primary School, Mr Atsuhiro plans to extend the bookshelf project to two additional schools in the Northern Province: Crusade Primary School and Bethel Primary School.

item.title: CS to focus on rehabilitation
item.description: The newly appointed Correctional Service Commissioner Noel Sarei was officially welcomed into office with a parade this morning at the Bomana training facility. He took office two months ago and will serve a four-year term.
item.content:encoded:
The newly appointed Correctional Service Commissioner Noel Sarei was officially welcomed into office with a parade this morning at the Bomana training facility.

He took office two months ago and will serve a four-year term.

In his welcome parade this morning, Commissioner Sarei outlined his key focus areas for his four-year term in office, with a specific focus on rehabilitation of detainees.

He pledged to work in addressing some of the legacy issues impeding the work of the Correctional Services in the country.

The Correctional Services, which continue to face many challenges while carrying out their mandated roles of containment and rehabilitation, are also changing their focus.

Commissioner Noel Sarei highlighted that among its rehabilitation programs is providing detainees with education so they can leave with tertiary qualifications after their prison terms are up.

He also said plans are in place for long-term offenders to be compensated adequately for the work they do.

Commissioner Sarei, whose key focus is on rehabilitation, is also singling out the welfare of female detainees and their children.

Training Commandant Chief Inspector Kiddy Keko welcomed Commissioner Sarei to inspect the parade.

Chief Inspector Keko highlighted the challenges that await the new commissioner, which include staff welfare, prison facilities, insufficient budgets and detainee rehabilitation.

Commissioner Sarei commended all his officers throughout the country, and in the 25 prison facilities, for the work they do amidst challenges.

He pledged to work with them in improving the Correctional Services across PNG.

With four years in office and the many challenges plaguing the Correctional Services, Commissioner Sarei is determined to restore confidence and trust in this important arm of the justice sector in the country.

item.title: Lands Department hands over lease title for new Huon district HQ
item.description: The Department of Lands and Physical Planning [DLPP] has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting district development across the country following the issuance of a state lease title to the Huon Gulf District Development Authority [HGDDA]. The land title for Portion 429, located along the 9 Mile–Bulolo Highway outside Lae city in Morobe, was officially presented to Huon Gulf MP and Minister for Co
item.content:encoded:
The Department of Lands and Physical Planning [DLPP] has reaffirmed its commitment to supporting district development across the country following the issuance of a state lease title to the Huon Gulf District Development Authority [HGDDA].

The land title for Portion 429, located along the 9 Mile–Bulolo Highway outside Lae city in Morobe, was officially presented to Huon Gulf MP and Minister for Community Development and Religion, Jason Peter . Peter accepted the title on behalf of the HGDDA and the people of Huon Gulf .

The allocated land will host the new Huon Gulf District Headquarters, an infrastructure project intended to boost administrative capacity and open up further development opportunities in the electorate .

DLPP Secretary Benjamin Samson said securing land titles for government institutions is vital for establishing long-term planning, investment, and public service delivery.

"The Department of Lands and Physical Planning is committed to supporting districts throughout the country by facilitating access to land and ensuring that development projects are built on a solid legal foundation," Samson said .

He said legal land ownership is necessary for districts to secure project funding and build essential infrastructure for local communities.

HGDDA representative and former Morobe Provincial Administrator Kemas Tomala expressed gratitude to the DLPP, stating that securing the title is an important step towards economic growth of the district and Morobe.

Samson assured that the department will continue collaborating with national, provincial, and district authorities to supply land for Papua New Guinea's socio-economic development agenda

item.title: Guns amnesty to end in 16 September
item.description: With just one month left before the National Firearms Amnesty ends on September 16, Police Minister Sir John Pundari is calling on national and provincial leaders to work closely with police and mobilize communities to surrender illegal firearms. The program has already seen more than 200 weapons handed in, particularly from Enga, with additional surrenders reported from surrounding Highlands and
item.content:encoded:
With just one month left before the National Firearms Amnesty ends on September 16, Police Minister Sir John Pundari is calling on national and provincial leaders to work closely with police and mobilize communities to surrender illegal firearms.

The program has already seen more than 200 weapons handed in, particularly from Enga, with additional surrenders reported from surrounding Highlands and East New Britain provinces.

Illegal firearm owners across Papua New Guinea have been reminded they have only one month left before the National Firearms Amnesty closes on Independence Day.

Minister Pundari said when the grace period for surrendering weapons expires, police will arrest anyone found in possession of illegal firearms after the deadline.

He said amnesty is the last opportunity for communities to hand in weapons voluntarily, before enforcement operations begin.

“I ask you all in the remaining 5-6 weeks, to come together as a nation and say no to illegal guns.” Sir John said.

Pundari commended the people of Enga province for their cooperation with police in surrendering more than 200 firearms.

He said this is a significant step towards peace and security. However, the Police minister is aware of some individuals who remain reluctant to give up their weapons.

“If you are still holding onto the illegal guns, treasuring it and not surrendering, there will be no tolerance,” he said.

The police minister warned that those holding onto illegal firearms are endangering their children’s future.

He urged the community leaders to act now and safeguard the next generation from the harm illegal guns can cause.

item.title: Festival’s legacy reflects strong culture in Ambunti
item.description: The successful conclusion of the 18th Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival in East Sepik reflects the deep-rooted cultural heritage of the people of Ambunti, local leaders say. Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk said strong cultural traditions and customs continue to play a pivotal role in maintaining social harmony and resolving community conflicts.
item.content:encoded:
The successful conclusion of the 18th Sepik River Crocodile and Arts Festival in East Sepik reflects the deep-rooted cultural heritage of the people of Ambunti, local leaders say.

Ambunti local level government [LLG] president Edward Wiruk said strong cultural traditions and customs continue to play a pivotal role in maintaining social harmony and resolving community conflicts.

Wiruk said local disputes in the area are predominantly settled through customary mediation long before law enforcement needs to intervene.

“The police ratio and crime rates in Ambunti are very low,” Wiruk said.

“Whenever problems arise, our people and police resolve conflicts in the traditional way. Law and justice interventions account for only about five per cent, as police actively leverage culture to mediate and restore peace.”

The Ambunti area comprises distinct language and cultural groups, including the Sepik Iwam, Wokomas, Hunstein, Nukuma-Koma, Manambu, Yambun, and Avatip communities.

Despite modern pressures, locals across these ethnic groups have preserved their traditional languages, customs, songs, and artistic heritage.

The three-day cultural showcase concluded peacefully in Ambunti, with local residents maintaining order and ensuring a safe environment for both domestic and international tourists.
